clue.text: Dash away to take photocopies

definitions.meaning: to dash away is to flee or leave in a hurry
to produce copies on a machine, as when printing off handouts

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off to the copier to make duplicates.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same phrasal verb: fleeing quickly, and printing off copies on a machine.

clue.text: Spanish king takes shelter on getting back

indicators.note: the Spanish king takes in the shelter, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: REY is Spanish for king
cover means shelter, as in taking cover

explanation.surface: A Spanish monarch hides away once he has been brought back home.
explanation.definitionFit: A return to health or the regaining of something lost is described by this noun.

clue.text: New delivery of Meissen is just due

indicators.note: a new delivery reorders the word Meissen, so its letters arrive in fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh consignment of Meissen porcelain is expected any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just due' reads as 'about to arrive', but it means a deserved comeuppance. MEISSEN is the German porcelain maker.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday use the word names a fitting retribution, the punishment someone deserves.

clue.text: Anticipation as set tea is laid out

parts.note: for can mean as, in 'taken for granted' or 'for example'

indicators.note: laid out means arranged afresh, so the words set tea are rearranged

explanation.surface: Looking forward to a meal as the tea table is prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' reads like a link word but supplies FOR; 'laid out' gives ETASTE, the tea-table picture hiding the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample that lets you anticipate what is coming.

clue.text: Showing off the monarch of aquatic birds

parts.note: swans are water birds; the singular serves as the attributive in a title like that of king
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: Royal pomp displayed by the ruler of the swans.
explanation.walkthrough: The king OF swans is written SWAN KING, so the clue's order flips in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Swanking is boastful behaviour, flaunting oneself to impress.

clue.text: A façade to attract custom

parts.note: literally the shop-front display set out to draw in customers, and figuratively any show put on for appearances

explanation.surface: A shop front dressed up to pull in shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both arranging goods in a shop's display and any superficial presentation meant to impress.

clue.text: Nearly time for bed

parts.note: the hours of darkness when bedtime approaches

explanation.surface: It is getting late and bedtime approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours of the day are when people go to sleep.

clue.text: I managed to get one article from the Middle East

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
I is the Roman numeral for one
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have acquired a single item from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing from Iran, a country of the Middle East, is described this way.

clue.text: Assemble in spring at Hereford

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits within the words spring at Hereford

explanation.surface: People gather for a springtime event in the cathedral city of Hereford.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford is an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to come together or collect, a synonym of assembling.

clue.text: They imitate others, such as Renoir and Monet

definitions.meaning: mimics who do impressions of famous people
French painters of the late nineteenth-century movement named after Monet's Impression, Sunrise

explanation.surface: Copycats and the French painters Renoir and Monet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both entertainers who mimic celebrities and painters of the Impressionist school.

clue.text: He shoots in the line of duty

definitions.text: He shoots in the line of duty

parts.words: He shoots in the line of duty
parts.note: reads like an armed officer firing at work, but the shooting is filming

explanation.surface: A policeman or soldier fires his weapon at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or television crew member shoots footage as his job.

clue.text: To transplant tissue is hard work

definitions.meaning: surgically moving skin or tissue from one place to another

explanation.surface: Surgery to move tissue is a laborious job.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the surgical term for implanting tissue and British slang for strenuous labour.

clue.text: He calls for force to resolve riot

parts.note: vis is Latin for force

indicators.note: to resolve the riot is to break it up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone summons the police to settle a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: VIS is Latin, a convention solvers meet often; 'to resolve' gives ITOR, the riot being settled only in its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: One who calls on someone, paying a visit, is a guest or caller.

clue.text: Not in the team? That's most unlikely

definitions.meaning: excluded, on the outer side of the selected group
as in an ... chance, a remote possibility

explanation.surface: A player's hopes of selection look remote.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means exterior or excluded, and also remote, as in a slim chance.

clue.text: Rebels demand higher wages

definitions.meaning: pay increases, in British usage pay ...

explanation.surface: Strikers demand more money.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a pay increase is a 'rise' (American 'raise').
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for revolting and the British noun for salary increases.

clue.text: Imposing cast includes a theologian

indicators.note: the throw takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to sling is to throw or cast
DD, Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: An impressive group of actors features a religious scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddling someone with a burden means imposing it on them.

clue.text: Most recent move by night watchmen, maybe

parts.note: late can mean most recent, as in 'the late election'
to shift is to move

explanation.surface: The newest change in the duties of the night guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers on the evening or overnight rota form this group, and night guards are an example.

clue.text: Resoundingly mournful news received by factory

indicators.note: the factory takes the news in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a plant is a factory
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Sad news arrives at the works and echoes around.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, plaintive sound, like a lament.

clue.text: One day in the past

explanation.surface: Once upon a time, or some day yet to come.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means at an unspecified time and, as an adjective, former.

clue.text: Waterproof paints offered to relations

parts.note: oils are oil paints
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: An artist's paints are handed to family members.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a waterproof coat made of oiled cloth.

clue.text: It could add up to a pound

definitions.text: It could add up to a pound

parts.words: It could add up to a pound
parts.note: a sum of coins reckoned together, which might come to one pound

explanation.surface: Loose change might amount to a quid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the sum of figures added together, whatever amount that comes to.

clue.text: Enter organisation without top-rate apprentice

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
an organisation of the letters of Enter puts them in a new arrangement

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-class

explanation.surface: A newcomer joins a company without top pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enter' looks like a verb but is the fodder; 'organisation' gives TRNEE, and 'without' in its old sense of outside wraps it round the first-class mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone learning a trade, like an apprentice.

clue.text: A manoeuvre needing diplomacy, I note

parts.note: tact is diplomacy
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A move that requires diplomatic skill, someone remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned move to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Bank's controller found near oil rig

indicators.note: to rig is to fix or arrange, so the letters near oil are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bank's executive is spotted close to an oil platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is not a financial bank but an aircraft tilting in a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: This hinged flap on an aircraft wing controls the roll, letting the plane tilt.

clue.text: Roam over the hills.

definitions.meaning: to wander across an area freely
a chain of mountains or hills

explanation.surface: Wandering across the uplands.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for wandering freely and a noun for a line of mountains.

clue.text: Under-secretary in disgrace needs support

indicators.note: the under-secretary is placed in the disgrace

parts.note: a stain on one's character is a disgrace
US is the abbreviation for under-secretary

explanation.surface: A disgraced government official needs backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to support or hold up.

clue.text: Army reservists know it's stolen

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
ken is Scottish for know

explanation.surface: Soldiers realise something has been stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken means seized or carried off, a synonym of stolen.

clue.text: During the prison term I gain awareness

indicators.note: during places the letter within the prison term

parts.note: a sentence is a prison term

explanation.surface: A prisoner becomes enlightened while serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to perceive and feel, a form of consciousness.

clue.text: Make short work of criminal of little brain

parts.note: con is short for convict, a criminal
dense means stupid

explanation.surface: Dealing quickly with a dim-witted crook.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'make short work of' is a disguise: the definition is just 'Make short'.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to shorten or compress.

clue.text: Bear witness at the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Someone gives evidence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to testify or certify that something is true.
